boot() registers a listener or takes a service from the container in 4 places. boot() runs once for every process of the server, so each of them is built on every request. registerEventListener() in register() builds a listener only when its event fires.
3 boolean columns are NotNull. Oracle cannot store false in such a column, so the server stops the migration with an exception. A boolean column needs notnull false.
Up to Nextcloud 32 the server checks this only where info.xml lists no database, or lists oci among them. From Nextcloud 33 on the server makes the column nullable on Oracle itself.

5 transactions are opened and closed by hand. The trait TTransactional has atomic() since Nextcloud 24 and atomicRetry() since Nextcloud 27, which repeats a transaction that ran into a deadlock, as the manual recommends.

3 timed jobs do not say whether they are time sensitive. A job that sets TIME_INSENSITIVE with setTimeSensitivity() is moved to the maintenance window of the server; whether a job is heavy enough for that only its maintainer knows.
lib/ reads the clock directly in 12 places. OCP\AppFramework\Utility\ITimeFactory, a PSR-20 ClockInterface, gives the same time and can be replaced in a test.

The app reads and writes its app config in 218 places and registers no config lexicon, which IRegistrationContext::registerConfigLexicon() takes since Nextcloud 31. A lexicon states the type, the default and the sensitivity of each key in one place.

1 place states routes that are no constants, so this cannot read them: the server builds them at run time. The inventory lacks them, and what depends on the full list of routes is left out: route-unreferenced, ocs-unreferenced, frontend-url-without-route, controller-method-unrouted and the operations of openapi-drift that no route provides.
